titulek: Russia attacks Ukraine with two missiles and 580 drones: 536 drones downed
titulekPuvodni: Russia attacks Ukraine with two missiles and 580 drones: 536 drones downed
shrnuti: Russia has launched two Kh-59 air-to-surface missiles and 580 drones since the evening of 14 October. Ukraine's air defences destroyed 536 drones, but strikes were recorded at 31 locations and debris fell at 11 others. The attack was still ongoing as of 08:00.

vyrez.text:
Ukraine destroys or jams 536 Russian drones during overnight attack | Ukrainska Pravda
A fire caused by a Russian attack in Kirovohrad Oblast. Photo: State Emergency Service of Ukraine
Russian forces have attacked Ukraine with two Kh-59 air-to-surface missiles and 580 drones of various types since the evening of 14 October. Air defence forces have managed to down 536 drones, but dozens of strikes have also been recorded. The attack is ongoing.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force
Quote: "As of 08:00, [Ukrainian] air defence forces had destroyed or jammed 536 Shahed, Gerbera and other types of drones. Hits by aerial assets have been recorded at 31 locations and the fall of downed aerial assets (debris) at 11 locations. The attack is ongoing, with several enemy drones still in Ukrainian airspace."

Skip to main content
Advertisement
EU lawmakers urged the bloc’s executive to robustly defend the International Criminal Court against U.S. sanctions in a letter sent to Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Tuesday and obtained by POLITICO. “We formally call for the urgent deployment of all instruments at our disposal to protect the International Criminal Court from the consequences of these sanctions,” reads the letter, signed by 58 MEPs, led by ECON chair and S&D lawmaker Aurore Lalucq and EPP Dutch lawmaker Dirk Gotink. They ask the Commission boss “to draw a clear line towards the US administration.”
The Trump administration has repeatedly threatened to demolish the ICC “brick by brick.” Washington has already sanctioned several judges, including judges from France, Italy and Slovenia, after the court issued an arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Tetiana and Mykola Musiienko. Photo: screenshot from Aliona Musiienko's Instagram
On the evening of 12 October, a high-rise building in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district was hit by a Russian drone just as Tetiana Musiienko and her husband Mykola were walking past. The 59-year-old kindergarten teacher was killed and her husband is in a serious condition.

Details: Aliona said her parents were right next to where the impact occurred. Mykola had met his wife from work, as he did every day, and they were walking home together. The couple were just 50 metres away from the apartment building where they lived.

Po ruských útocích zahynuli v Charkově čtyři lidé, informoval v úterý šéf oblastní správy Oleh Syněhubov. Ruské drony útočily i v jiných částech Ukrajiny. Podle šéfa regionální správy Mykolajivské oblasti Heorhije Rešetilova bezpilotní stroje poškodily třeba nákladní terminál v přístavním městě Mykolajiv. Naopak Ukrajina v noci na úterý měla cílit na ruský Stavropolský kraj, kde trosky sestřeleného dronu poškodily průmyslovou zónu v Něvinnomyssku, tvrdí tamní gubernátor Vladimir Vladimirov.
Syněhubov oznámil, že Rusové v pondělí v pozdních večerních hodinách zaútočili na civilní infrastrukturu Charkova deseti střelami. Zasáhli několik bytových a rodinných domů. V troskách byla do rána objevena čtyři těla.

titulekPuvodni: Ruská ambasadorka musela u Bulharů na kobereček. Vinit Rusko z útoků v Černém moři je podle Sofie „logické“
shrnuti: „Logika napovídá, že výsledek hraje ve prospěch Ruské federace,“ vysvětlil bulharský premiér Rumen Radev, proč si Sofie předvolává ruského ambasadora. Jde o nové dronové útoky u pobřeží Černého moře, které podle Radeva zasáhly další dvě nákladní lodě a jednu z nich potopily.

vyrez.text:
Ruská ambasadorka musela u Bulharů na kobereček. Vinit Rusko z útoků v Černém moři je podle Sofie „logické“ — Deník N
Bulharsko žádá NATO o pomoc s vyšetřováním útoků a o posílení vzdušných a námořních hlídek v Černém moři. Ilustrační foto: ImageBank4U, Adobe Stock
„Logika napovídá, že výsledek hraje ve prospěch Ruské federace,“ vysvětlil bulharský premiér Rumen Radev, proč si Sofie předvolává ruského ambasadora. Jde o nové dronové útoky u pobřeží Černého moře, které podle Radeva zasáhly další dvě nákladní lodě a jednu z nich potopily.
Více o poslechu Deníku N
Obě nákladní lodě útočné drony zaměřily nedaleko bulharského pobřeží, oznámil dnes Radev.
První z nich „zasáhly tři vzdušné drony“, popsal bulharský premiér. Tuto loď identifikoval jako Ukrajinou vlastněné plavidlo, které plulo pod jménem Chelsea 3 a maltskou vlajkou.
Šestnáct zachráněných
Na palubě se nacházela patnáctičlenná posádka tvořená sedmi Ukrajinci a osmi Ázerbájdžánci. Všechny se podařilo z moře zachránit, sdělil Radev. Pět námořníků utrpělo lehčí zranění a jsou v péči lékařů, zbylí jsou v pořádku.
Ohledně druhé zaměřené lodi byl premiér na informace skoupější. Plavidlo bylo „zasaženo“ a potopeno…

Ruský raketový útok na Charkov si vyžiadal najmenej troch mŕtvych a jedenásť zranených. Záchranári pátrajú po ľuďoch, čo môžu byť zasypaní v troskách bytového domu.
Najmenej traja ľudia zahynuli a 11 ďalších sa zranilo pri ruskom vzdušnom útoku na ukrajinský Charkov. V utorok to potvrdili miestne úrady. TASR o tom informuje podľa agentúry DPA.
Podľa informácií regionálnej správy zasiahol raketový útok štvorposchodovú bytový dom. Pod troskami môžu byť stále uväznení živí ľudia a na mieste zasahujú záchranári.

Německá policie zadržela už třetího člověka v souvislosti se zapálením polské stanice satelitního internetu Starlink. Polské úřady za sabotáží vidí ruské tajné služby. Napadená infrastruktura zajišťuje spojení také pro Ukrajinu.
Článek
Nachází se asi 40 kilometrů pod Varšavou, ve vesnici s 280 obyvateli uprostřed zahrad, chráněná plotem z vlnitého plechu. Kolem pobíhají slepice.
Stanice satelitní sítě Starlink v Polsku má podobu několika bílých kopulí ukrývajících satelitní antény. Nenápadná instalace uprostřed polského venkova má přitom strategický význam. Jde o pozemní stanici satelitního internetu společnosti SpaceX amerického miliardáře Elona Muska.
Přes zdejší infrastrukturu prochází internetové spojení využívané také na Ukrajině. Starlink je tam důležitý pro úřady,…

The French navy intercepted and boarded an oil tanker linked to Russia’s so-called shadow fleet in the Indian Ocean, President Emmanuel Macron announced Monday.
The French joint staff said naval inspectors boarded the vessel to verify its nationality after doubts arose over its claimed Benin registration. The operation took place around 450 nautical miles south of Réunion Island, an overseas territory of France.
Macron said the ship — the DF Peak — was suspected of sailing under a false flag and being involved in illicit fuel transportation. The vessel is under U.S., EU, U.K. and Ukrainian sanctions.
The tanker was being escorted to Réunion for further checks, said armed forces minister Catherine Vautrin.
The DF Peak is at least the sixth shadow-fleet tanker French authorities have detained over the past year, according to the exiled outlet The Insider.

France seizes Russian ‘shadow fleet’ oil tanker in Indian Ocean
October 13, 2026, 7:22 am
Source: Emmanuel Macron
France’s navy detained an oil tanker called the DF Peak that belongs to the “shadow fleet” on October 12, French President Emmanuel Macron said.
The tanker was detained more than 450 nautical miles south of Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean. Authorities suspect it was flying a false flag and illegally transporting fuel.
According to  data from Marinetraffic, the tanker was sailing under Benin’s flag and was headed to the port of Cruz Grande in Chile. It wasn’t clear where the vessel had sailed from.
The magazine Maritime Executive writes that the tanker was built in 2006 and originally belonged to the company Sovcomflot, sailing under the name NS Captain . It was renamed Kaliningrad in 2024 and took its current name in 2025. Its operator is now a company based in Hong Kong.
Maritime Executive also says that Benin’s national registry, whose flag the tanker flies, was once “considered a haven for Russia-linked shadow fleet vessels.” The U.S. sanctioned the tanker in February…

The European Security Council would fast-track traditional EU bureaucratic gridlock during security emergencies. Under the proposal, it would rely on what European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called a "counter-hybrid playbook" to address grey-zone hostile actions.

titulekPuvodni: Woman injured and house damaged in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district in Russian attack
shrnuti: A woman has been injured when debris from a drone damaged a house and its garden fence in eastern Kyiv on the morning of 13 October. Emergency services were dispatched to the scene, with no casualties mentioned in the initial reports.

vyrez.text:
Woman injured and drone debris damages two-storey house in Kyiv's Darnytskyi district | Ukrainska Pravda
A drone. Stock photo: Getty Images
A woman has been injured as a result of a Russian attack on Kyiv's Darnytskyi district on the morning of 13 October. Drone debris has damaged a two-storey house and its garden fence.
Source: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko ; Kyiv City Military Administration
Quote from Klitschko: "Drone debris has damaged a two-storey house and its garden fence in the Darnytskyi district. Emergency services are on their way to the scene."
Advertisement:





Details: Kyiv City Military Administration had previously said that, according to early reports, debris had fallen on the grounds of a house in the Darnytskyi district.
The reports did not mention any casualties.
Update: Kyiv City Military Administration later confirmed that a woman had been injured as a result of a Russian strike on a house. She is receiving the necessary medical treatment.
Background: Russian forces attacked a residential building in Kyiv with a drone on the evening of 12 October, killing two people and injuring others.

Russian forces launched a large-scale missile attack on Kharkiv on Oct. 12, injuring at least 11 people, including an emergency responder, and damaging residential buildings across the city, according to Ukrainian authorities.
Three people trapped beneath the rubble were later rescued, UNIAN reported , citing Ukraine's State Emergency Service.
Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Syniehubov said Russian forces had reportedly used 10 Banderol-type missiles in the attack, targeting civilian infrastructure.
In the city's Kholodnohirskyi district, a strike hit a four-story residential building, destroying an entire section. At least 10 nearby private houses were also damaged, Syniehubov said.

Source: The Wall Street Journal
Alexus Grynkewich at a forum in Warsaw, October 12, 2026

General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, said NATO forces would destroy “anything and everything” involved in any Russian attack on the alliance’s territory. He presented his “theory of victory” at a security conference in Warsaw.
Bloomberg reported a week earlier that Grynkewich would present a “quick victory” strategy for responding to a Russian advance on the alliance’s eastern flank. Reuters reported that he did not explicitly mention Russia in his speech, but his message was clearly directed at the Kremlin.
Grynkewich said NATO is a defensive alliance but will thwart, repel, and crush any attacks on its members:
If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight.…

October 12, 2026, 3:36 pm
Source: RFE/RL
RFE/RL’s Balkan Service and the investigative project Sistema have identified a diplomat at the Russian Embassy in Serbia who was declared persona non grata in Bulgaria in 2021 during an investigation into explosions at weapons depots.
Alexander Krasiy, an assistant military attaché, held the same position at the Russian Embassy in Bulgaria before moving to Serbia. In April 2021, Bulgaria’s Foreign Ministry said it was expelling a Russian diplomat but did not name him. The news agency Zona News and Bulgarian National Television identified him as Krasiy.

shrnuti: Hundreds of stores were targeted by the overnight hack, which spoiled fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.

vyrez.text:
Fridges in French supermarkets hit by cyber attack - BBC News
Image source, AFP via Getty Images
By Ian Aikman
Published
1 hour ago
Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros.
Hackers reportedly gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight.
The chief executive of Coopérative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack.
More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while at least 300 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand were affected, according to the AFP news agency.
Intermarché said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported.
Some supermarket staff reportedly said they were hit by waves of hot air when they opened freezer units on Monday morning.

Hits by aerial assets have been recorded at 15 locations and downed aerial assets (debris) landed at four locations.
The Air Force warned that the Russian attack is ongoing.

titulekPuvodni: Strikes on Yandex data centres disrupt over 80 Russian services
shrnuti: Three Ukrainian drone attacks on Yandex data centres disrupted more than 80 digital services, while bot traffic from the company's network fell to almost zero.

vyrez.text:
Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centres disrupt over 80 services | Ukrainska Pravda
Stock photo
Three consecutive Ukrainian drone attacks on data centres operated by Russian technology company Yandex have caused disruptions to more than 80 of its digital platforms and third-party but related services, such as banking apps and ride-hailing services. Bot traffic from the Yandex network has also fallen to almost zero.
Source : Tom's Hardware , citing Cloudflare data
Details : Tom's Hardware reported that on 8 October, when a Yandex data centre in Sasovo housing two supercomputers was damaged, bot traffic from the network fell to around 57% of its peak level. On 9 October, a larger Yandex data centre complex in Kaluga was put out of operation, followed by another facility in Vladimir on 11 October . As a result, bot traffic fell to 0.4% of the peak level recorded over the previous two weeks.

Zlata's aunt, police officer Yuliia Malysh, was injured and remains in hospital in a serious condition. Yuliia's husband, 47-year-old police veteran Oleh Malysh , and her mother, Liudmyla, were killed in the attack.

Quote: "On the night of 7-8 October (from 18:00 on 07 October), the enemy attacked [Ukraine] with 142 Shahed-type attack drones (82 of which were jet-powered), Gerbera UAVs and Parodiya-type decoy drones from the following areas: Oryol, Kursk and Shatalovo, Russia, and occupied Donetsk and Hvardiiske in occupied Crimea."

Early reports indicate that as of 09:30, air defence had intercepted 126 enemy Shahed-type UAVs, Gerbera and drones of other types."
Details: Hits were recorded at seven locations and intercepted aerial assets (debris) fell at four locations.
The aerial attack is being repelled by aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, electronic warfare assets, unmanned systems units and mobile fire groups from Ukraine's defence forces.

shrnuti: Russia's hostile activities cost the UK an estimated £2-2.5 billion a year, including losses from cyberattacks and damage to undersea infrastructure.

Russian sabotage costs UK up to £2.5bn a year | Ukrainska Pravda
Photo: Getty Images
The economic impact of Russia's hostile activities against the United Kingdom amounts to at least £2-2.5 billion a year, according to a new report by the vice-chair of the All-Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) on rearmament.
Source: Financial Times
Details: The new report, entitled " The Putin Tax ", estimates the costs of the disruption, recovery and investment in resilience caused by Russia's hybrid warfare against the UK.
Advertisement:





However, the study by Labour MP Graeme Downie, published on Wednesday 7 October, suggests that the true figure is likely to be " vastly higher " than his estimate. He warned that gaps in government-published data make it impossible to accurately calculate the cost of hybrid warfare linked to Moscow.
The overall estimate of £2-2.5 billion comprises three components: £400-500 million in average annual losses from major incidents since 2022, such as attacks on Jaguar Land Rover, the Royal Mail and National Health Service suppliers; £1.47 billion in losses from Russia-linked cyberattacks, based on industry analysis and threat intelligence; and £250-500…

An investigation into a large-scale incursion of Russian drones into Polish airspace in September 2025 has been closed because those responsible could not be identified.
Source: Lublin District Prosecutor's Office; European Pravda, citing RMF24
Details: The military prosecutor's office spent months investigating the attack, trying to establish who was responsible.

Russia’s hybrid attacks across Europe — cyberattacks, sabotage, drone incursions — have been ramping up in recent months. But European governments are quietly preparing for something much worse.
On today’s show, Zoya Sheftalovich and Ian Wishart discuss how EU ambassadors have been meeting in recent weeks to discuss what to do if a potential Russian hybrid attack were to result in mass casualties.
Next, Britain’s minister in charge of relations with Europe, Hamish Falconer, is making his first official visit to the European Parliament. Zoya was able to catch him on the phone to ask him more about EU-U.K. relations under PM Andy Burnham and a potential deal on farming, among other things, currently in the works.
Finally, what may sound like the plot of a spy novel is in fact real news coming out of Berlin where Germany’s former spy chief has been arrested on suspicion of espionage.

Zum Schutz vor Spionage und Sabotage darf die Bundeswehr Netzwerferdrohnen kaufen. Das entschied der Haushaltsausschuss im Bundestag. Auch neue Feuereinheiten für das "Patriot"-Luftverteidigungssystem billigte er.
Die Bundeswehr darf zum Schutz ihrer Kasernen und Gebäude sogenannte Netzwerferdrohnen anschaffen. Das beschloss der Haushaltsausschuss des Bundestages, wie das Verteidigungsministerium mitteilte. Netzwerferdrohnen werfen Abfangnetze aus, mit denen Drohnen vom Himmel geholt werden können. Somit können sie laut Ministerium auch in Städten eingesetzt werden.
"Netzwerferdrohnen gelten als bewährte Abwehrmaßnahme für den Liegenschaftsschutz", hieß es. Sie können demnach vor Spionage- und Sabotagedrohnen schützen und werden meist zusammen mit Störsendern und Radar eingesetzt. Hintergrund der Anschaffung sei die steigende Bedrohungslage durch Klein- und Kleinstdrohnen, auch für Ausspäh- und Sabotageversuche, im In- und Ausland.

Lawyers for a Ukrainian ex-military officer accused of leading the bombing of Russia 's Nord Stream pipeline in September 2022 argued at the start of his trial in Germany on Wednesday that "an aggressor's infrastructure " may have been a lawful target .

Source: Meduza
The number of users reporting outages in Sberbank’s services has sharply increased in Moscow, St. Petersburg, the Novosibirsk region, and other regions, according to data from the monitoring sites Sboi.rf and Downdetector.
Users reported that online banking was not working, payments were not going through, the website would not load, and the app would not open.
Outages were also reported on other sites and services: Mail.ru, Kontur, Ozon, MegaFon, and VKontakte, as well as the provider SkyNet St. Petersburg.
Ukrainian drones attacked a Sberbank data center in Balakovo, in the Saratov region, overnight on October 14. Sberbank First Deputy Chairman Alexander Vedyakhin confirmed the attack but said all services were operating normally.

Latvian authorities have formally declared Riga-based Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin persona non grata, local media reported, and Ragozin himself confirmed on Wednesday.
Latvian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Līga Jermacāne told the outlet Delfi that an unidentified Russian national was added to the persona non grata list last Wednesday. Foreign Ministry adviser Toms Sadovskis said the basis for the decision will be withheld for “national security” reasons.
On Wednesday, Ragozin confirmed that he was notified of his expulsion the day before.
Ragozin claimed he was blacklisted in retaliation for his critical reporting and commentary on Western policy and far-right political networks.
He argued that Latvia intentionally declared him persona non grata to prevent him from appealing his expulsion in Latvian courts.
